Hi Priya — attaching the first draft packet for FinServ review. Highlights: 

1) Packet contents (attached):
- firebreak_network_sketch_v1.pdf — one‑page annotated diagram showing: public edge (TLS termination), tenant‑egress gateway, aggregation layer (WAF/load‑balancer), tenant enclave (isolated compute pools), control plane (private control plane endpoints), and outbound egress proxy. Zones are color coded: orange (edge), blue (aggregation), green (tenant enclave), purple (control plane).
- private-deploy-segmap.svg — high fidelity segmentation map for engineering; includes example ACL snippets for cross‑tenant blocking and allowed monitor flows.
- soc2-evidence-index.csv — index mapping artifacts to SIG/SOC2 questions (Network and Infrastructure families prioritized).

2) Key isolation controls (summary):
- Tenant fencing: each customer runs in logically separated compute pools backed by per‑customer routing tables and VM network namespaces; KV cache and model weights do not cross tenant boundaries.
- Control plane separation: control plane endpoints are reachable only from management subnets and authenticated via mTLS; operational traffic flows are audited to a write‑once logstore with HSM‑backed signing.
- Egress / outbound filtering: egress is routed via customer-configurable proxy or our managed egress gateway; default deny posture for all outbound except approved destinations.
- KMS/HSM: keys for private deployments can be customer‑provided (BYOK) or managed; we document key envelope flows and HSM attestation artifacts in the packet.

3) Notes on evidentiary artifacts we can provide on short notice:
- ACL exports (redacted) 
- Control plane audit digest sample (last 30 days)
- Diagram source (SVG) and PNG/PDF renderings

Please review and flag any SIG question IDs that need priority mapping. If helpful we can redact customer‑specific names from the ACL exports prior to sharing.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 20m call if you want to walk through the diagram.

Best,
Kimberly Park
